head: Afloat16:perf/smoothap-positive-ranks-20261115
title: Reduce SmoothAP rank storage to positive candidates
body:
## Problem

SmoothAP builds an `N × N × N` comparison tensor although only positive query/candidate ranks contribute to average precision. With a fixed number of examples per class, most of that storage and backward work is unused.

## Change

Calculate ranks only for the `P` positive pairs belonging to valid queries, using `P × N` comparisons. Each pair still ranks against the entire batch. The self-inclusive positive convention, candidate self-comparison mask, singleton-query handling, and miner weights are preserved. Half-precision per-query accumulation uses float32 before restoring the output dtype.

Add a retained-autograd-storage regression, all-one-class reference coverage, and differentiable-zero cases for empty/singleton/all-unique batches. Update the loss documentation, numerical design notes, and release notes.

## Validation

[Successful isolated validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/pytorch-metric-learning/actions/runs/43665623560) checks the exact source/test/documentation blobs in `c7fe549083aaa0b832d9185642f12c26cceb6b00` against upstream `b95a42310f50720a766b91008470b278364f705d`.

- The new storage test fails on unchanged upstream: 8,621,056 retained bytes exceed its 2,097,152-byte budget; it passes with the change.
- Focused value, gradient, distance-matrix, and composition coverage: **44 tests and 272 subtests passed**.
- Complete CPU suite: **1,531 tests and 2,485 subtests passed; 10 tests deselected**.
- Ruff formatting/lint, ty, strict MkDocs, scoped Code Polishy checks, dependency review, and the post-install supply-chain check all passed.

Values and gradients match the existing independent float64 reference within its dtype-specific tolerances; no bitwise-equivalence guarantee is intended.

### Same-run CPU comparison

Ubuntu 24.04.5, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 running on CPU, one Torch thread, float32 embeddings of dimension 32. Both implementations use the same inputs and settings. Timings are median forward+backward times after two warmups and five alternating measurements.

| Batch / examples per class | Before → after ms | Retained saved-tensor bytes before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 64 / 4 | 3.408 → 0.693 | 1,119,744 → 123,648 |
| 128 / 4 | 22.372 → 1.517 | 8,637,440 → 443,904 |
| 256 / 4 | 307.319 → 3.160 | 68,032,512 → 1,674,240 |
| 64 / 64 | 1.014 → 2.361 | 1,119,744 → 1,705,728 |

The byte counts measure unique storages retained by autograd, **not system or GPU peak memory**. The one-class case still has `P = N²`, remains cubic, and has extra indexing overhead; this optimization targets batches with sparse positive pairs. The validation workflow stays on a separate fork branch and is not included in this PR.
